newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share surge takes index to record high.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share surge takes index to record high.

text.p: Nigerian shares surged again on Tuesday in heavy trading, pushing the all-share index to a record high, dealers said.
The index closed at 7474.04 from 7398.29 on Monday.
Traders said several sectors were seeing more activity than in the last couple of months because of growing interest in shares.
"Among sectors where shares have begun to rise recently is the industrial/domestic products sector," said one dealer.
Good results posted by Industrial Gases Plc, the sector leader, saw its price make robust gains since last month, as did Vitafoam and Aluminium Manufacturing Company (Alumaco).
Industrial Gases remained strong, closing 20 kobo up on Tuesday at 13.80 naira. Vitafoam and Alumaco finished five kobo up, respectively at 3.95 naira and 2.50 naira.
Cadbury led food shares in a bull run, adding 50 kobo to close at 28.50 naira.
Also firmer were Nestle, 50 kobo higher at 59.00 naira, and Nigerian Bottling Company, 40 kobo stronger at 39.50 naira.
First Bank was 40 kobo higher at 11.60 naira while Union Bank and UBA each gained 20 kobo to close at 10.05 naira and 8.80 naira, respectively, on strong demand.

Sustained interest in oil marketers saw African Petroleum hit 53.83 naira with a 1.03 naira gain. Agip was 80 kobo up at 27.10 naira, Mobil up 50 kobo at 58.50 naira and Total closed at 66.50 naira, adding 20 kobo.
Conglomerate PZ continued its downward slide, closing 30 kobo lower at 26.70 naira.
But Lever Brothers rose again by 35 kobo to 18.00 naira.
Paint makers were poor finishers. Berger Paints shed five to 4.45 naira while African Paints lost one kobo at 1.51 naira.
Brewers had a respite as Nigerian Breweries and Guinness were unchanged at 15.80 naira and 7.60 naira, respectively.
